context.body: Prayer first appears within danger, promise, judgment, confession, and one person speaking for another. The bounded source is Genesis 20:1–18.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Abraham is told to pray for Abimelech.
observations.label: Abraham is required to pray for Abimelech: action

observations.body: the narrative later reports his prayer and the household’s healing.
observations.label: Abraham is required to pray for Abimelech: response

payload.posture: Read Genesis 20:1–18 as calling, fear, and intercession evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: God commands the intercession before the narrative reports Abraham praying and the household being healed; the passage does not explain why the prophet’s prayer is required after the warning.
payload.title: Abraham is required to pray for Abimelech
